name: Ekambareswarar Temple
story: One of Kanchipuram's grand Shiva temples, Ekambareswarar is linked with the earth element and is known for its large complex, towering gopuram, pillared spaces, and sacred mango-tree legend.
didYouKnow: It is one of the Pancha Bhoota Sthalams, associated with the element earth.

name: Kanchipuram Silk Weaver Street
story: A living craft street where looms, dyed silk threads, family workshops, and patient handwork reveal why Kanchipuram sarees became part of wedding and festival memory.
didYouKnow: Traditional silk sarees can take several days or weeks depending on design complexity.

name: Kamakshi Amman Temple
story: Kamakshi Amman Temple is one of the city's most important Shakti shrines, drawing pilgrims into a sacred centre where goddess worship, ritual, and Kanchipuram's identity meet.
didYouKnow: The temple is closely associated with the goddess Kamakshi, one of the most revered forms of Devi in Tamil tradition.

name: Kailasanathar Temple
story: Kailasanathar Temple is among the finest early Pallava monuments in Kanchipuram, admired for sandstone architecture, sculpted shrines, and a quieter, more ancient atmosphere.
didYouKnow: It is often highlighted as one of the oldest surviving structural temples in Kanchipuram.

name: Varadharaja Perumal Temple
story: A major Vishnu temple in Chinna Kanchipuram, Varadharaja Perumal Temple is known for vast prakarams, sculpted halls, sacred tanks, and Divya Desam tradition.
didYouKnow: The temple is famous for the Athi Varadar festival, when the wooden image of the deity is brought out after long intervals.

name: Ulagalantha Perumal Temple
story: Dedicated to Vishnu as Trivikrama, this temple carries the story of Vamana measuring the worlds and is counted among the sacred Divya Desam temples.
didYouKnow: The complex is associated with multiple Divya Desam shrines within its precincts.

name: Vaikunta Perumal Temple
story: A Pallava-era Vishnu temple known for its layered architectural plan, historical panels, and royal visual storytelling carved into stone.
didYouKnow: Its sculptural panels are valued for what they suggest about Pallava royal history.

name: Kachabeswarar Temple
story: Kachabeswarar Temple is a Shiva temple with layered local tradition, set close to Kanchipuram's busy sacred core and temple-street life.
didYouKnow: The temple name is linked with the Kurma, or tortoise, form in local sacred storytelling.

name: Kumarakottam Murugan Temple
story: Kumarakottam is a Murugan temple placed within the sacred geography of Kanchipuram, connecting Shaiva, Shakti, and Murugan worship routes.
didYouKnow: It is traditionally visited along with nearby major temples in the city centre.

name: Chitragupta Swamy Temple
story: A distinctive temple dedicated to Chitragupta, the divine accountant in Hindu tradition, making it one of Kanchipuram's unusual and memorable sacred stops.
didYouKnow: Chitragupta worship is comparatively rare, which makes this temple stand out for many travellers.

name: Yathothkari Perumal Temple
story: Also known as Sonna Vannam Seitha Perumal Temple, this Divya Desam is tied to the idea of the deity responding to the devotee's word.
didYouKnow: The temple is linked to Alvar devotional tradition and Kanchipuram's Vaishnava heritage.

name: Ashtabujakaram Temple
story: A Vishnu temple known for the eight-armed form of the deity, Ashtabujakaram adds another rich layer to Kanchipuram's Divya Desam circuit.
didYouKnow: Its name refers to the deity's eight arms, a striking iconographic form.

name: Muktheeswarar Temple
story: A smaller Shiva temple that rewards slow exploration, Muktheeswarar shows how Kanchipuram's heritage is spread across many quiet sacred corners.
didYouKnow: Smaller temples like this help reveal the city's dense sacred geography beyond the famous landmarks.

name: Kanchi Kudil Heritage House
story: Kanchi Kudil presents the feel of a traditional Kanchipuram house, helping visitors imagine domestic life, local objects, and cultural memory beyond temple walls.
didYouKnow: It is often treated as a heritage stop for understanding old-town life and traditional interiors.

name: Pandava Thoothar Perumal Temple
address: Pandavaperumal Koil Street, Periya Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu 631502
timings: Usually morning and evening darshan; check locally before visiting
story: A Divya Desam connected with Krishna as the messenger of the Pandavas, this temple is remembered for its large seated deity and its link with Mahabharata storytelling.
didYouKnow: It is traditionally counted among the older Vishnu temples of Kanchipuram, along with Ulagalantha Perumal and Yathothkari Perumal.

name: Deepa Prakasar Perumal Temple
timings: Usually morning and evening darshan; check locally before visiting
story: Also known as Vilakkoli Perumal Temple, this Divya Desam is associated with Vishnu as the radiant light and with the birthplace tradition of Vedanta Desika nearby.
didYouKnow: The name Deepa Prakasar means the deity who shines like a lamp.

name: Pavala Vannar Temple
address: Pavala Vannar Koil Street, Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu
timings: Usually morning and evening darshan; check locally before visiting
story: A Vishnu temple celebrated in the Divya Desam tradition, Pavala Vannar is linked with the coral-hued form of the deity and Kanchipuram's dense Vaishnava sacred map.
didYouKnow: The temple is often visited together with other nearby Divya Desam shrines in the old town.

name: Azhagiya Singar Perumal Temple
timings: Usually morning and evening darshan; check locally before visiting
story: A Divya Desam dedicated to Narasimha, Azhagiya Singar Perumal Temple adds a powerful Vishnu story to Kanchipuram's temple network.
didYouKnow: Thiruvelukkai is one of the sacred Kanchipuram Divya Desam sites associated with Alvar hymns.

name: Nilathingal Thundam Perumal Shrine
address: Inside Ekambareswarar Temple complex, Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu
timings: Follows temple complex timings; check locally before visiting
story: A rare Vishnu Divya Desam shrine located within the Ekambareswarar Temple complex, linking Shaiva and Vaishnava traditions in one sacred space.
didYouKnow: Its legend connects Vishnu, Shiva's crescent moon, and the protection of Parvati during penance.

name: Aadhi Varaha Perumal Temple
address: Near Kamakshi Amman Temple, Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu
timings: Usually morning and evening darshan; check locally before visiting
story: A Divya Desam shrine associated with Vishnu's Varaha form, set close to the Kamakshi temple area and important to Kanchipuram's sacred geography.
didYouKnow: The shrine is part of the compact old-town temple circuit around Kamakshi Amman Temple.

name: Matangeswarar Temple
story: A smaller Shiva temple that helps reveal Kanchipuram beyond its biggest monuments, Matangeswarar belongs to the city's quieter sacred landscape.
didYouKnow: Kanchipuram's old town is filled with smaller shrines that preserve local ritual memory.

name: Jurahareswarar Temple
timings: Often listed as morning and evening hours; check locally before visiting
story: Jurahareswarar Temple is a distinctive Shiva shrine associated with healing from fever and disease, and is valued for its early Dravidian temple character.
didYouKnow: The name comes from Jvara, Hara, and Ishvara, meaning Shiva as the remover of fever.

name: Iravatanesvara Temple
story: A lesser-known Shiva temple associated with Kanchipuram's old sacred fabric, Iravatanesvara rewards travellers interested in quieter stone shrines.
didYouKnow: The name is linked with Airavata, the mythic white elephant of Indra, in temple tradition.

name: Trilokyanatha Jain Temple
story: An 8th-century Jain temple in Thiruparuthikundram, also called Jain Kanchi, showing that Kanchipuram's sacred history includes Jain heritage as well as Hindu traditions.
didYouKnow: The temple is dedicated to Jain Tirthankaras and is associated with Pallava-period patronage and later expansions.

name: Prakash Silks and Sarees
story: A well-known Kanchipuram silk showroom on Gandhi Road, popular for wedding silk sarees and a wide variety of traditional designs.
didYouKnow: It is frequently recommended in shopping guides for Kanchipuram silk sarees.

name: A.S. Babu Sah
story: A locally known silk shop often associated with traditional Kanchipuram saree buying and busy wedding-season shopping.
didYouKnow: Many travellers prefer comparing multiple silk shops before choosing zari, border, colour, and price range.

name: Nalli Silks Kanchipuram
story: Nalli is a heritage silk name associated with traditional sarees, festive collections, and classic Kanchipuram design language.
didYouKnow: Nalli's wider brand history dates back to the early twentieth century.

name: Pachaiyappas Silks
story: Pachaiyappas is a long-running Kanchipuram silk name, known for large silk collections and a heritage identity tied to the city.
didYouKnow: The brand traces its Kanchipuram silk trade story to 1926.

name: K.V. Rajaram Silks
story: A silk store on T.K. Nambi Street presenting pure silk sarees, wholesale options, and a family craft identity.
didYouKnow: The store highlights decades of experience and pure silk collections.

name: RMKV Silks Kanchipuram
story: RMKV is known for Kanchipuram pattu sarees, bridal silk, korvai borders, and design-led silk collections.
didYouKnow: Pure Kanchipuram sarees are commonly checked through Silk Mark and zari purity information.

name: Local Food Spots of Kanchipuram
address: Around Gandhi Road, Nellukara Street, and bus stand food lanes
timings: Best explored morning breakfast time and evening snack time
story: A premium hidden-gem trail for tasting Kanchipuram beyond famous temples: small tiffin shops, filter coffee corners, evening snacks, and local sweet stops.
didYouKnow: Food discovery works best by walking slowly through old streets and asking for the day's fresh local special.

name: Sarvatirtha Tank
timings: Best during early morning or calm evening hours
story: A peaceful storytelling stop where water, ritual memory, and old-town silence create a slower side of Kanchipuram away from crowded temple entrances.
didYouKnow: Temple tanks often acted as sacred, social, and environmental spaces in old South Indian towns.

name: Old Residential Streets
address: Old-town lanes around Kamakshi Amman and Vaikunta Perumal Temple areas
timings: Best explored in daylight; respect residential privacy
story: Quiet streets, threshold art, shaded houses, small shrines, and everyday rhythms show how heritage continues in ordinary local life.
didYouKnow: The most memorable Kanchipuram details are sometimes not monuments, but house fronts, doorways, and street-corner shrines.

name: Local Markets
address: Around Gandhi Road, Kamarajar Street, and old bazaar lanes
timings: Best during morning shopping hours and early evening
story: A lively hidden-gem experience for flowers, fruits, small shops, saree browsing, temple items, street snacks, and the everyday sound of the city.
didYouKnow: Markets are often the easiest place to understand how pilgrimage, shopping, food, and local life overlap.

name: Premium Walking Routes
address: Suggested old-town loop around temples, tanks, markets, and residential lanes
timings: Best before noon or after 4 PM
story: A premium route idea that combines quiet lanes, temple edges, food stops, markets, and local storytelling into one slow city walk.
didYouKnow: Walking routes reveal connections between places that are missed when each stop is visited separately.

name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
story: Meenakshi Amman Temple anchors Madurai with towering gopurams, ritual movement, and a city rhythm shaped by devotion and trade.
didYouKnow: The temple is one of the strongest visual symbols of Tamil temple architecture.

name: Madurai Food Street
story: This walk follows the smell of jigarthanda, hot snacks, and late-night food culture that keeps Madurai awake.
didYouKnow: Madurai's food streets are often busiest after sunset.
